I have farmed a long time, and at my age I do not want to spread myself too thin or gamble on a very risky plan. I will keep the land mainly on the crops I know can bring cash and that fit my well irrigation, with chili taking the biggest share because it matches my usual cabbage-chili-cabbage pattern and I know how to manage it. I will still plant cucumber, eggplant, and kidney bean, but on smaller areas so the work stays manageable for my family, especially since some people work off-farm. I will use better seed on the crops where stable yield matters most, put fertilizer on in moderate amounts instead of pushing too hard, irrigate enough to protect yield, and keep tillage simple with rotary tillage because my land is small and I need to save labor. I will control pests on chili, cucumber, and eggplant more closely because they are more sensitive, and I will keep kidney bean lighter in inputs because it is easier and lower-cost for me to manage.
